1.  **Determine the geometry of the overlap:**
    The fold removes a triangular section of length 4 from the main horizontal span. Due to the $45^\circ$ angle, the vertical rise is also 4. The strip then folds back horizontally to form the top section.

2.  **Analyze the lengths:**
    Let the width of the overlapping vertical section (where $P$ and $Q$ interact) be $w$.
    The bottom layer has a total length of 13. It covers the flat part, the diagonal gap (4), and the overlap part ($w$).
    So, the length of the flat part for $P$ is $13 - 4 - w = 9 - w$.
    The top layer starts $w$ units from the end. It covers the overlap and then extends to the left. The length available for this extension is the total length (13) minus the overlap width ($w$).
    So, the length of the horizontal part for $Q$ is $13 - w$.

3.  **Define the Areas:**
    The height of the strip is 4.
    Area $P = \text{width} \times \text{height} = (9 - w) \times 4$.
    Area $Q = \text{width} \times \text{height} = (13 - w) \times 4$.

4.  **Solve for $w$:**
    Given $P = 2Q$:
    $$4(9 - w) = 2 \times 4(13 - w)$$
    Divide by 4:
    $$9 - w = 2(13 - w)$$
    $$9 - w = 26 - 2w$$
    Add $2w$ to both sides:
    $$9 + w = 26$$
    $$w = 17$$

5.  **Calculate $x$:**
    From the diagram, $x$ represents the length of the horizontal top section of rectangle $P$.
    $x = 9 - w = 9 - 17 = -8$.
